after.title: Preprint: Effects of age and lesion characteristics on chronic outcomes after childhood stroke: a large-scale study of 469 childhood stroke survivors
after.authors: Griffis, J. C.; Bruss, J.; Mhanna, A.; Brzus, M.; Fullerton, H. J.; Wintermark, M.; Dlamini, N.; Hills, N. K.; Dowling, M. M.; Lo, W.; Bernard, T. J.; Jordan, L. C.; Mackay, M.; Lehman, L.; Kirton, A.; Cummings, D. D.; Lee, S.; Taylor, J. M.; Fox, C. K.; Boes, A. D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Pediatrics, Carver College of Medicine, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, USA
after.abstract: The effects of stroke on the developing brain are thought to depend on age at stroke onset, but the nature of this relationship is unclear. While it has been suggested that younger age at stroke onset might facilitate recovery, there is also evidence that critical developmental periods in early childhood confer increased vulnerability to injury. Associations between age at stroke onset and childhood stroke outcomes are mixed and often inconsistent, and the roles of lesion factors such as size, laterality and location are poorly understood. We investigated how age and lesion factors relate to chronic (6+ months post-onset) sensorimotor, expressive language, receptive language, and cognitive/behavioral impairments in 469 childhood stroke survivors enrolled in the SCOUTS study (median age at stroke=9.3 years; 57% male). We used ordinal logistic regression models to characterize associations between outcomes and age at stroke onset, left and right hemispheric lesion volumes, and years to chronic assessment, and we used voxel-based lesion-symptom correlations to evaluate associations with lesion location. We also tested whether age at stroke onset moderates relationships between lesion factors and chronic outcomes. When considered in isolation, younger age at stroke onset was significantly associated with worse outcomes across all domains, but in multivariable models, statistically significant associations were observed only for language outcomes. Larger lesion volumes in each hemisphere were significantly associated with worse contralateral sensorimotor outcomes and with worse language and cognitive/behavioral outcomes. For language outcomes, associations with lesion volume were strongest for the left hemisphere, and older age at stroke onset amplified the detrimental effect of large left hemisphere lesions on expressive language outcomes. Lesion-symptom analyses mapped sensorimotor impairments to structures including the putamen, sensorimotor cortices, superior parietal cortex, and cortico-spinal projections. Expressive and receptive language impairments both mapped to mostly left-lateralized and partially overlapping frontal, temporal and parietal structures, with the strongest associations in the white matter underlying left posterior temporo-parietal areas. Cognitive/behavioral impairments mapped to bilateral regions associated with action mode and somato-cognitive action networks including right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, left inferior frontal and supramarginal gyri, and inter-effector nodes of the right pre-central gyrus. These results provide novel insights into how age at stroke onset and lesion factors contribute to childhood stroke outcomes, map domain-level impairments to specific lesion locations, and indicate that the vulnerability of left hemisphere language networks to injury may increase as language becomes more left-lateralized during development.

after.title: Preprint: Predicting pediatric stroke outcomes using adult lesion-symptom models
after.authors: Griffis, J. C.; Bruss, J.; Mhanna, A.; Brzus, M.; Fullerton, H. J.; Wintermark, M.; Dlamini, N.; Hills, N. K.; Dowling, M. M.; Lo, W.; Bernard, T. J.; Jordan, L. C.; Mackay, M.; Lehman, L.; Kirton, A.; Cummings, D. D.; Lee, S.; Taylor, J. M.; Fox, C. K.; Boes, A. D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Pediatrics, Carver College of Medicine, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, USA
after.abstract: Lesion location is a key predictor of post-stroke outcomes in adults, but its relevance for predicting childhood stroke outcomes is unclear. Recent developmental neuroscience work suggests that the gross spatial organization of large-scale brain systems may be generally conserved across development, raising the possibility that damage to common anatomical substrates might underlie chronic domain-level impairments after both adult-onset and childhood stroke. If so, then it should be possible to leverage adult lesion-symptom relationships to predict chronic childhood stroke outcomes. We tested the hypothesis that lesion-symptom models trained to predict sensorimotor and language impairments in patients with adult-onset brain lesions can be translated to predict chronic sensorimotor and language outcomes after childhood stroke. We trained multivariate lesion-symptom models to predict sensorimotor (Grooved Peg-Board Test: N=463; median age=53.6, IQR=17.9 years) and language (Token Test: N=379; median age=53.2, IQR=19.4 years) impairments in patients with adult-onset brain lesions. We applied the trained models to lesion segmentations from childhood stroke survivors enrolled in the SCOUTS Study (N=469; median age=9.3, IQR=11.0 years), resulting in outcome predictions that we compared against chronic (6+ month) measures of sensorimotor and language impairment derived from the Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure and the Recurrence and Recovery Questionnaire. The adult lesion-symptom models generated outcome predictions that robustly correlated with pediatric impairment scores (sensorimotor: rho=0.43; language: rho=0.42; PFWE <0.001), enabled classification of pediatric impairment status (both AUC=0.76; PFWE=0.004), and afforded unique predictive power in multivariable pediatric outcome models (sensorimotor: adjusted OR=3.6, 95% CI=2.4-5.2; language: adjusted OR=3.0, 95% CI=1.67-5.30). Lesion-symptom models trained using pediatric lesion and outcome data captured robust lesion-symptom relationships (both rhocv=0.40, P<0.001), but yielded no advantage over the adult model predictions when compared directly via cross-validation in the pediatric cohort. Further, the adult and pediatric models made similar predictions when applied to the same lesion data even after adjusting for common effects of lesion size and laterality, suggesting a general convergence towards common anatomical signals present in both children and adults. Lesion-symptom models trained in patients with adult-onset brain lesions can be translated across outcome measures and developmental stages to predict chronic sensorimotor and language impairments after childhood stroke. These results establish lesion location as an important predictor of childhood stroke outcomes, demonstrate the feasibility of translating adult lesion-symptom models for chronic outcome prediction in children, and support the broader conclusion that the critical anatomy underlying post-stroke sensorimotor and language impairments may be generally conserved across development.

after.title: Preprint: A new diagnostic pipeline for recurrent diffuse podocytopathies post transplantation using glomerulus-on-a-chip technology
after.authors: Gage, A. M.; Mason, W. J.; Perin, L.; Da Sacco, S.; Loucaidou, M.; Briggs, J.; Chandler, J. C.; Price, K. L.; Long, D. A.; Salama, A. D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University College London Centre for Kidney and Bladder Health
after.abstract: Introduction: Recurrent diffuse podocytopathies in kidney transplants are a leading cause of graft loss with poorly understood pathophysiology and variable response to therapy. Recent work has focussed on anti-slit diaphragm antibodies, but reliable methodology for their detection has proven challenging. In addition, antibody-associated disease only accounts for disease mechanism in a proportion of patients. Clinicians need a reliable stratification pathway, firstly, to determine if a circulating factor indiscriminate of its nature is present, and secondly, to establish whether it is antibody-associated or otherwise, to facilitate a precision medicine approach to therapeutic management and transplantation. Methods: This exploratory cohort study used primary glomerular cells within a modified Glomerulus-On-A-Chip (GOAC) model. To identify the presence of a pathogenic circulating factor, we exposed the GOAC to an inception cohort of healthy control (n=4), non-recurrent (n=4) and recurrent disease sera (n=14); assessing permeability by the addition of fluorescein isothiocyanate conjugate (FITC) albumin. To determine if recurrent disease was antibody-associated or otherwise, immunostaining was performed on sera-exposed GOACs and post-recurrence allograft biopsies. Subsequently, we validated our pipeline on six sera blinded to clinical outcome. Results: GOAC exposure with all recurrent disease sera resulted in an increase in albumin permeability compared with healthy controls. The mean fold difference between recurrent and non-recurrent disease sera permeability was 3.42 (p <0.001). An anti-nephrin antibody-associated pattern was found by immunostaining for 9/13 (69%) recurrent disease sera and was consistent with individual clinical response to antibody-targeted therapy. ROC curve analysis showed excellent sensitivity and specificity of our pipeline (AUC 0.977, p <0.0001) which accurately predicted clinical outcomes for all six patients in the blinded validation cohort. Conclusions: This functional GOAC pipeline accurately determines the presence of a pathogenic circulating factor and can define it as anti-nephrin-associated or otherwise to guide therapeutic strategy and optimise approaches to transplantation.

after.title: Preprint: Causal Emergence of Macroscopic Stochastic Dynamics from a Multi-modal Foundation Model of Human Sleep
after.authors: Liu, Y.; Nie, G.; Sun, Y.; Zhang, H.; Zhang, J.; Wang, Z.; Yang, M.; Ye, J.; Li, D.
after.abstract: Sleep is an essential, self organizing physiological state conserved across species, yet its macroscopic coordination remains governed by unknown physical principles. For nearly sixty years, clinical medicine has classified sleep into heuristic, discrete 30 second epochs, an empirical convention that flattens continuous non-equilibrium dynamics and leaves deep subcortical neuromodulatory control fundamentally unobservable. Although emerging artificial intelligence foundation models can decode multimodal physiology with high accuracy, their high-dimensional representations remain uninterpretable black boxes, leaving the generative laws of sleep unformulated. Here we show that, across four independent multinational cohorts, causal emergence analysis of a multimodal foundation model condenses human sleep into a single continuous order parameter whose dynamics are well described by a Landau Ginzburg jump diffusion equation. This trajectory is physiologically structured: its overnight variance follows an AASM stage hierarchy (Wake, NREM, REM), and its diffusion shape tracks apnea hypopnea severity. Bidirectional clinical perturbations further support the decomposition: continuous positive airway pressure lowers baseline diffusion and apnea band spectral excess while shallowing the late-night potential well, whereas GABAergic agonism reduces the true jump rate and nocturnal awakenings without deepening the well. Length matched comparisons under dexmedetomidine sedation deepen the well and suppress jumps relative to natural sleep. By replacing empirical classification with an explicit stochastic description, our work uses a foundation model as a probe of physiological dynamics rather than only as a predictor and treats human sleep as an analytically tractable physical system. More broadly, the finding that multi-organ coordination during sleep can be summarized by a low dimensional order parameter suggests a general route from opaque artificial intelligence representations to testable macroscopic models of the subcortical dynamics that sustain human consciousness and fail in neuropsychiatric disease.

after.abstract: Precise delineation of stroke lesions on MRI scans provides essential quantitative information used routinely in stroke rehabilitation research. Manual annotation continues to be the gold standard for stroke lesion delineation but is subjective and labor-intensive. Our previous release of ATLAS v2.1 (N=1271) provided a large, open-source dataset of T1w stroke brain MRIs and manually segmented lesion masks, which facilitated the development of numerous lesion segmentation algorithms. However, fully automated algorithm performance is not yet adequate to replace manual protocols; existing lesion segmentation algorithms still lack accuracy and generalizability. As model architectures grow increasingly sophisticated, they demand large-scale, diverse training data. Here, we present ATLAS v3.0 (N=1815), an updated, larger dataset of T1w stroke brain MRIs with corresponding manually segmented lesion masks. ATLAS v3.0 comes with nearly 43% more data, consisting of a publicly accessible, heterogenous training (n=1453), and a hidden generalizability dataset with subjects that remain unreleased (n=362). We anticipate this updated ATLAS v3.0 release will support the growing data demands of advanced lesion segmentation algorithms.

after.title: Preprint: Decreased thermal contrast sensitivity for paradoxical heat sensation in diabetic polyneuropathy
after.authors: Mitchell, A. G.; Fischer Ehmsen, J.; Kraenge, C. E.; Courtin, A. S.; Brask-Thomsen, P. K.; Gylfadottir, S. S.; Fardo, F.
after.abstract: Paradoxical heat sensation (PHS), the perception of warmth during cooling, is typically induced by alternating warm and cold stimulation. Recent work has demonstrated that thermal contrast, defined as the difference between alternating temperatures, is a key determinant of this phenomenon in healthy individuals. However, it remains unclear whether peripheral sensory loss changes the thermal contrast required to elicit PHS and whether the experience itself remains the same after such sensory loss. We investigated PHS in individuals with probable diabetic polyneuropathy (DPN; N = 32) and healthy controls (N = 42) using a pre-registered Bayesian computational model. The model related the probability of a warm report to thermal contrast and used response times and confidence ratings as markers of perceptual uncertainty. Although prevalence was similar between groups, the thermal contrast required to elicit PHS was higher in patients with DPN, reaching the midpoint of the psychometric function at approximately 51% thermal contrast in healthy controls and 80% in patients with DPN. In both groups, warm reports were accompanied by greater uncertainty, reflected in longer response times and lower confidence. This pattern suggests that PHS does not typically reflect a clear sensation of warmth but rather an ambiguous thermal experience. These findings show that the sensation is accompanied by perceptual uncertainty in both groups, while patients with DPN require greater thermal contrast to elicit it.

after.authors: Carlomagno, F.; Bonetti, L.; Rosso, M.; Brattico, E.; Taurisano, P.; Biasi, M. M.; Tancredi, G.; Manni, A.; Iaffaldano, A.; Paparella, G.; Gasparre, D.; de Tommaso, M.; Bevilacqua, V.; Paolicelli, D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Electrical and Information Engineering, Polytechnic University of Bari, Bari, Italy
after.abstract: The auditory P300 is widely used at the sensor level to study cognitive dysfunction in multiple sclerosis (MS), but its brain generators have rarely been investigated. The three-stimulus oddball separates task relevance from stimulus rarity, and source-level network analysis can show where and when this distinction is altered. We recorded magnetoencephalography (MEG) in 20 MS patients and 15 healthy controls during a three-stimulus auditory oddball with standard, target and non-target tones. Broadband networks were estimated from beamformer source activity with BROAD-NESS, a principal component analysis of group-averaged sources. Groups were compared with cluster-based permutation tests corrected across networks. Four networks explained 94% of the variance. Sensory (N1m) and P3 responses and task performance did not differ between groups. In a bilateral perisylvian and sensorimotor network, the difference between target and non-target responses was smaller in patients than in controls at about 370 to 500 ms (cluster p = 0.020, corrected across networks; Hedges' g = -1.11 and Bayes factor 16.1 in the localizer window). A conventional source-by-source analysis of the same contrast found no cluster surviving correction. The effect was robust to leave-one-out analysis, an alternative network estimation and excluding participants with clinical or recording characteristics, but did not survive correction across all three contrasts (p = 0.108). Network measures were not related to discrimination performance or fatigue, and no exploratory correlation with clinical or cognitive measures survived correction. In MS, task-related source-level networks were largely preserved, but one network differentiated less between task-relevant and task-irrelevant deviants, without a behavioural deficit.

In a bilateral perisylvian and sensorimotor network, the difference between target and non-target responses was smaller in patients than in controls at about 370 to 500 ms (cluster p = 0.020, corrected across networks; Hedges' g = -1.11 and Bayes factor 16.1 in the localizer window). A conventional source-by-source analysis of the same contrast found no cluster surviving correction. The effect was robust to leave-one-out analysis, an alternative network estimation and excluding participants with clinical or recording characteristics, but did not survive correction across all three contrasts (p = 0.108). after.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) is a marker of astrocytic activation that correlates with cerebral Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology. The causal relationship between GFAP elevation and amyloid-{beta} remains unclear. We examined whether A{beta} drives GFAP elevation and whether GFAP is independently associated with AD progression. METHODS: In the Harvard Aging Brain Study (HABS; n=329 cognitively unimpaired participants) and the Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project (ROSMAP; n=835 deceased participants spanning cognitively unimpaired to dementia), we performed one-sample Mendelian randomization. APOE {epsilon}4 served as the instrumental variable to estimate the causal effect of A{beta} (PET in HABS; immunohistochemistry in ROSMAP) on GFAP (plasma in HABS; brain mRNA expression in ROSMAP). Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models assessed GFAP associations with tau, hippocampal atrophy, and cognitive decline. RESULTS: In both cohorts, Mendelian randomization supported a causal effect of A{beta} on GFAP (HABS {beta} = 0.37; 95% CI, 0.11 to 0.63; P=6.1x10-3; ROSMAP {beta} = 0.35; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.59; P=3.3x10-3). In HABS, GFAP associations with tau and cognition were no longer significant after adjusting for A{beta}, and GFAP was not associated with hippocampal atrophy. In ROSMAP, GFAP remained associated with tau and cognition after A{beta} adjustment, but not with cognition after additional adjustment for tau. DISCUSSION: Brain GFAP gene expression and plasma GFAP elevation may be downstream consequences of A{beta} accumulation. GFAP showed little independent association with cognition once core AD pathology was accounted for. These findings refine the interpretation of elevated plasma GFAP in AD.

after.authors: Patel, H. J.; Muqtadir, S. A.; Choi, C.-H.; Shaikh, U. J.; Oros-Peusquens, A.-M.; Shah, N. J.; Moran, C. N.; Ietswaart, M.; Binkofski, F.
after.abstract: Background/Hypothesis Concern is growing around the effects of repeated non-concussive head impacts from football heading, but it is unclear whether a single bout of heading alters neurochemistry. Neurometabolite levels were measured with 7 T proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy with the primary motor cortex before and after controlled heading. Methods In a within-subject, repeated measures study, 20 participants (15 male; mean [SD] age of 25.2 [6.6]), with no reported history of head injury in the past year or any neurological conditions, performed 20 controlled rotational headers. Proton spectra were acquired at three timepoints: one before heading (Pre) and twice after heading (Post_1 and Post_2). Neurometabolite absolute molal concentrations (mol/Kg) were used as the main outcome. Results N-acetylaspartate (NAA) showed a significant effect of Time [F(2, 36.7) = 8.01, pFDR < 0.01] with elevated levels at the Post_2 timepoints compared with both Pre and Post_1 measurements. No other metabolites showed significant changes. Conclusion An acute bout of 20 headers was associated with detectable changes in NAA concentration levels. This finding from 7 T MRS provides valuable insight into the neurochemical changes resultant from repeated non-concussive head impacts, which may be suggestive of an acute neuronal response to heading. This study was registered with the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00029600)

after.title: Preprint: Effects of human lactoferrin combined with low-dose iron on iron status, hair and skin in women: a randomized, double-blind pilot study
after.authors: Vasenina, E.; Evans, C.; Chau, M.; Barney, D. E.; Peterson, R.
after.abstract: Background: Iron deficiency is common in women of reproductive age, frequently occurs without anemia, and is often accompanied by fatigue and hair shedding. Lactoferrin (LF), an iron-binding glycoprotein, may support iron absorption without the hepcidin response provoked by higher-dose iron, but a human-equivalent LF (heqLF) produced by precision fermentation has not been tested in a randomized trial. Objective: To examine the effects of two doses of heqLF combined with low-dose iron on iron status, inflammation, hair shedding, and participant-reported wellness in women with low ferritin. Methods: In this randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, decentralized pilot study, 31 women aged 18 to 64 years with ferritin <35 ng/mL were randomized to 100 or 50 mg/d of heqLF, each with 5 mg/d of iron as ferrous bisglycinate, for 6 weeks; 27 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Iron, hematological, and inflammatory biomarkers were measured at Weeks 0, 2, 4, and 6, and hair shedding (self-administered modified hair pull test) and participant-reported outcomes were assessed weekly. Results: Ferritin, the primary endpoint, did not change in either group (100 mg: +0.9%; 50 mg: +11.3%; both P [≥] 0.34). With both groups combined, total iron-binding capacity decreased by 17 mcg/dL, unsaturated iron-binding capacity by 34 mcg/dL, and transferrin by 13 mg/dL (all adjusted P [≤] 0.028), whereas increases in serum iron and transferrin saturation were not statistically significant in the primary analysis. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein and hemoglobin did not change. Hair pull counts decreased by 62% with 100 mg (adjusted P = 0.017) and by 39% with 50 mg (adjusted P = 0.039). Participant-reported wellness and hair scores improved in both groups, and skin scores improved with 100 mg only. No outcome differed between doses. Conclusions: In women with low ferritin, 6 weeks of heqLF with low-dose iron was accompanied by lower iron-binding capacity and transferrin, consistent with improved iron availability, as well as reduced hair shedding and improved wellness, without a change in ferritin. Because the study had no placebo or iron-only control arm, these exploratory findings warrant confirmation in a larger placebo-controlled trial. Clinical trial registration: www.clinicaltrials.gov, identifier NCT07953972

after.title: Preprint: Biased and variable: pictorial blood loss estimates from photographs of used menstrual pads compared with alkaline hematin
after.authors: Apsey, A. N.; Awais, A.; Burnett, D.
after.abstract: STUDY QUESTION: How accurate and how variable are lay raters' estimates of menstrual blood loss when they apply a pictorial blood loss assessment chart (PBLAC) to photographs of used pads? SUMMARY ANSWER: Raters captured only about 62% of the blood measured by alkaline hematin, classified only 47.1% of their ratings of heavy cycles as heavy and gave estimates that varied substantially between raters and between sessions. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Pictorial charts are widely used to estimate menstrual blood loss, but their accuracy against alkaline hematin varies, and it is unclear how consistently different people score the same product. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Cross-sectional online study of reliability and agreement with a repeated assessment, conducted in November 2026 according to a written protocol. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Sixty-nine women recruited through social media rated photographs of the same 117 used pads from eight cycles of a validation study in which every pad had been measured by alkaline hematin, and 44 repeated the ratings about 2 weeks later. The pad users' own in-hand scores served as a comparator. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Raters' cycle estimates captured 62% (95% CI 60-65%) of the alkaline hematin volume (mean bias -44.1 ml; 95% limits of agreement -100.5 to +12.3 ml), and sensitivity for heavy menstrual bleeding (>80 ml) was 47.1%. Choosing the picture closest to each pad's alkaline hematin volume would have produced a shortfall equal to 58% of the raters' shortfall, and the users' in-hand scores were also low (mean bias -38.2 ml). Krippendorff's alpha was 0.86 (95% CI 0.82-0.89) and the test-retest intraclass correlation 0.90, but in absolute terms raters' estimates of the same cycle had a pooled between-rater SD of 18.4 ml (up to 32.1 ml for a single cycle); among the 44 raters who repeated the task, the within-rater SD was 10.7 ml, and 6% of classifications changed on retest. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: A limited number of cycles were chosen from the original study to represent different cycle volumes; had other cycles been chosen, the results might have been better or worse. All pads were of one brand, only two cycles were not heavy, and raters scored photographs rather than handling pads. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: With the pictogram evaluated here, scoring of pad photographs systematically underestimated blood loss, partly because of the chart's fixed picture volumes, and estimates of the same cycle differed by tens of millilitres between raters and between sessions. High agreement statistics should not be taken as evidence that a chart accurately identifies blood loss above 80 ml per cycle. STUDY FUNDING/COMPETING INTEREST(S): This study was funded by the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development of the National Institutes of Health (NIH grant R44HD102235-03, awarded to TheraNova). A.Aw. and D.B. are co-founders of Quantiflow, which develops image-based methods for measuring menstrual blood loss, including the algorithm evaluated in the source study of the photographs used here. Quantiflow currently operates as a project of TheraNova, which holds the NIH grant that funded this study. Quantiflow is expected to be incorporated as an independent company in which A.Aw. and D.B. will hold equity. A.Aw. and D.B. have been compensated by TheraNova within the past 36 months. D.B. is a named inventor on a pending patent application related to Quantiflow's image-analysis algorithm. All other authors declare no competing interests. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

after.authors: Puri, S.; Greenlund, L.; Ross, D.; Huang, P.; Pokala, S.; Agyekum, R.; Kamson, D. O.; Hope-Lucas, C.; Redmond, K.; Sair, H.; Kleinberg, L. R.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Neurosurgery, Oregon Health & Science University
after.abstract: Purpose/Objectives: IDH inhibitor therapy is now FDA-approved for low-grade IDH-mutated (mIDH) gliomas. Early studies with short follow-up periods have reported variable tumor volume reduction. We describe radiographic responses in long-term responders. Materials/Methods: MRIs in patients with progressive mIDH[LK1.1] gliomas treated with targeted therapy for >36 months from 2019-2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Contouring of T2/FLAIR sequences were performed to calculate tumor volumes. Results: From total 49 consecutive patients started on targeted therapy, 13 were included (11 astrocytoma, 2 oligodendroglioma). Total 157 MRI were analyzed. All were on treatment with ivosidenib. Median duration of treatment was 59.5 months (range 37.4-79.3) with 1/13 offered chemoradiation due to radiographic progression. Pretreatment tumor volume increased at the rate of 12.6 cc/year (p = 0.0007) but declined during the first year of therapy at the rate of -9.73 cc/year (p < 0.001). Afterwards, the slope was no longer significantly different from zero (p = 0.36). Conclusions: Our real-world data demonstrates a reduction in tumor volume during the first year of treatment of progressive mIDH glioma with ivosidenib followed by prolonged stabilization. The principal benefit of mutant IDH inhibition may not be prolonged tumor volume reduction but durable stable disease. Our findings can inform clinical practice using targeted therapy over an extended period which is currently unreported.

after.title: Preprint: Feasibility of the Oldenburg phrase test (OLPHRA) in cochlear-implant users
after.authors: Urban, A.; Holube, I.; Ibelings, S.; Puschmann, S.; Radeloff, A.; Sandmann, P.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Division of Clinical Audiology, Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, University Medical Centre Oldenburg, Oldenburg, Germany
after.abstract: The Oldenburg Phrase Test (OLPHRA) is a novel speech-recognition test utilizing a fixed matrix structure of four-word everyday phrases delivered via a synthesized female voice. This prospective, observational study evaluated the feasibility and clinical utility of the OLPHRA during early rehabilitation and compared it against established clinical standards, namely the Freiburg Monosyllabic Speech Test (FMST) and the Oldenburg Sentence Test (OLSA). Fifteen newly implanted cochlear implant (CI) users were tracked longitudinally at one, two, and four weeks post-activation, and compared to a cohort of fourteen experienced CI users. To index cognitive demand and listening effort during active perception, verbal response times (VRT) and task-evoked pupil dilations were recorded simultaneously. Speech-recognition scores for the newly implanted cohort improved significantly over the four-week period, and did not differ significantly from those of the experienced users at week four, with ceiling effects for both matrix-style tests. However, FMST scores were significantly poorer in both groups. The OLPHRA evoked significantly shorter log-transformed VRTs than the OLSA, indicating faster behavioural processing. In the exploratory pupillometric analysis, a growth curve model revealed a significantly steeper initial pupillary slope for the OLPHRA than for the OLSA, which may indicate faster recruitment of cognitive resources during phrase encoding. Taken together, these findings support the clinical feasibility of the OLPHRA for tracking auditory rehabilitation in the early post-activation period. VRTs and pupil dilation showed diverging patterns that warrant further study. (trial registration: German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS), URL: https://www.drks.de/DRKS00040892, registration number: DRKS00040892)

after.title: Preprint: Osteosarcopenia and its impact on falls in older patients in Vietnam
after.authors: Nguyen, T. V.; Mai, D. T. T. B.; Dao, M. T.; Vu, T.; Nguyen, C. L. K.; Ngangue, P.; Woodward, M.; Nguyen, T. N.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The George Institute for Global Health, Australia
after.abstract: Background and aim: Osteosarcopenia, the concurrent presentation of osteoporosis and sarcopenia, can increase the risk of physical trauma and functional decline in older adults. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of osteosarcopenia, its associated factors, and its impact on falls among older hospitalised patients in Vietnam. Methods: This prospective observational cohort study included patients aged 60 years or older admitted to the Department of Geriatric Medicine at a hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Participants were followed for 3 months post-discharge to record incident falls. Multivariable logistic regression was applied to examine the factors associated with osteosarcopenia, and the relationship between osteosarcopenia and falls. Results are presented as odd ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: There were 243 participants (64.6% female). They had a mean age of 75.0 years (SD 8.6 years). The prevalence of osteosarcopenia was 42.0%. Age (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.09), female sex (OR 9.75, 95% CI 4.57-20.82), and underweight (OR 2.48, 95% CI 1.03-5.96) were associated with greater odds of having osteosarcopenia. The OR relating osteosarcopenia and falls after 3 months was 2.76 (95% CI 1.20-6.37) before adjustment and 2.11 (95% CI 0.82-5.39) after accounting for age, sex, rural/urban living and comorbidities. Conclusions: Osteosarcopenia was highly prevalent among older hospitalised adults in Vietnam and was associated with increased odds of falls. Clinicians should consider screening for osteosarcopenia in older adults, particularly among women and those who are underweight.

after.title: Preprint: Cost-effectiveness of generic semaglutide for Status First Nations adults with obesity and prediabetes under British Columbia's Plan W
after.authors: Curry, T. E.; Kovalko, I.; Stockdale, J. E.; Spackman, E.
after.abstract: Background: British Columbia's Plan W could cover generic semaglutide for Status First Nations adults with obesity and prediabetes. Its value for money is unknown. Methods: We modelled lifetime public costs and quality-adjusted life-years for adults with obesity and hemoglobin A1c of 6.0% to 6.4% who added semaglutide 1 mg to usual care, using the best available Canadian diabetes costs (Alberta and Ontario). After stopping, everyone returned to usual diabetes risk. In addition, the cases avoided on treatment either stayed avoided (100%), mostly stayed avoided (83%, from one-year trial data), or all occurred within a year (0%). Results: At 83%, treatment gained 0.124 quality-adjusted life-years and cost $4,250 (Alberta) or $16,297 (Ontario-derived) per quality-adjusted life-year. At 0%, costs were $39,500 and $46,376. At 100% with Alberta costs, spending fell by $38. Conclusions: Generic semaglutide is likely a cost-effective way to postpone diabetes. Whether it pays for itself is uncertain.

after.title: Preprint: Potential public health and economic impact of influenza and COVID-19 multicomponent vaccination (mRNA-1083) for adults aged 65 years and older in France
after.authors: Mehta, D.; Biron, L.; Carette, J.; Demont, C.; Gavazzi, G.; Guerin, O.; Leleu, H.; Reynaud Levy, O.; Rozaire, O.; Uhart, M.; Van de Velde, N.; Beck, E.
after.abstract: Seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 continue to cause substantial disease burden, particularly among older adults. The potential public health and economic impact of introducing combined enhanced influenza/COVID-19 vaccine, mRNA-1083, was assessed, for adults [≥]65 years, versus separate high-dose inactivated influenza vaccine (HD-IIV) and BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccination. A static decision-tree health economic model for France evaluated five value dimensions with mRNA-1083, in a stepwise approach, during an average post-pandemic season. Health system efficiencies, potential improved protection versus current comparators, avoidance of influenza egg-adaptation effects, and increased vaccine coverage rates (VCR) were assessed in the base case, and a future-looking scenario assessed potential reduced strain mismatch from antigenic drift, due to later influenza strain selection enabled by the mRNA platform. During an average season, mRNA-1083 was estimated to potentially prevent 25,830 medically-attended cases and 4,286 hospitalisations, saving EUR69.4 million in healthcare costs. Replacing separate influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations with mRNA-1083 may generate health system efficiencies, including 439,285 healthcare-provider hours saved. Potential improved clinical protection with mRNA-1083 prevented 2,194 hospitalisations saving EUR11.8 million in treatment costs. Avoiding egg-adaptation effects prevented a further 75 influenza hospitalisations, saving EUR0.3 million. Increased VCR with mRNA-1083 prevented an additional 2,017 hospitalisations, saving EUR10.4 million. Later strain selection could reduce antigenic drift and prevent a further 148 influenza hospitalisations and EUR0.6 million treatment cost on average per season. Results support that mRNA-1083 may improve seasonal respiratory vaccination by combining convenience, health system efficiency and potential for improved protection, higher coverage, and better influenza strain matching in a single injection.

after.title: Preprint: How many large language models does title-abstract screening need? Theory, two replications and an evaluation at real prevalence
after.authors: Quinelen, E.; Neumann, I.; Contreras, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Health Technology Assessment and Evidence-Based Health, Ministry of Health of Chile
after.abstract: Background and Objectives: Researchers increasingly combine large language models (LLMs) to screen titles and abstracts, assuming that more models make screening safer. We estimated how many models a screening ensemble needs, given correlated errors, and tested the answer on independent reviews and at real prevalence. Methods: We modelled correlated votes with a beta-binomial model and estimated, by bootstrap, the smallest ensemble capturing 95% of the net-benefit gain attainable over the best single model, accounting for human reading time and machine cost. Eleven LLMs from four developers voted blind on records from 13 SYNERGY reviews (derivation). We tested predictions fixed in advance on 10 and 16 Cochrane reviews from a public screening benchmark (replications) and evaluated a two-voter pipeline with an adjudicator on 11 complete benchmark collections and six reviews published in 2026. Results: Errors on relevant records were correlated (intraclass correlation 0.56 among eight different models; 0.75-0.78 among roles or copies of one model): eight models carried the information of about 1.6 independent ones. In derivation, the best single model, pair and trio reached sensitivities of 0.920, 0.975 and 0.981. Three or fewer models captured 95% of the attainable gain in at least 86%, 88% and 80.8% of bootstrap replicates of every scenario in the derivation set and the two replications, respectively. Six of seven registered predictions held in replication 1 and three of five sealed predictions in replication 2, where a fourth model added 2.1 percentage points to trios on average but 0.3 to the best trio. At real prevalence, the pipeline sent 94 of 96 included studies to human reading in the benchmark collections and 163 of 178 in the 2026 reviews (12.1% of 12,196 records sent to reading); its more sensitive voter alone sent 259 of 274 with 12.0%, at under a quarter of the machine cost. Conclusion: Because LLM errors are correlated, our results suggest two or three well-chosen models may suffice, but this needs deeper exploration in future studies. Which models are combined and how matter as much as how many, and any ensemble should be compared with its best single member.

after.title: Preprint: MedDx, a training-free AI phenotyping model, identifies alcohol use disorder in cirrhosis with hepatologist-level agreement
after.authors: Wang, H.; Chen, Y.; Arif, M.; Pal, D.; Xiong, C.; Liu, H.; Liangpunsakul, S.; Desai, A. P.; Tu, W.; Gawrieh, S.; Su, J.
after.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is often under-documented in patients with cirrhosis, which delays treatment. Expert chart review of clinical notes can identify under-documented AUD, but is not scalable. We propose MedDx, an open-weight, training-free, and engine-agnostic language model, to phenotype AUD using clinical notes in patients with cirrhosis. We benchmarked MedDx on a 485-patient study cohort sampled from the 14,406-patient Indiana Cirrhosis Registry, using a chart-review-based reference as ground truth. MedDx agreed with the ground truth at three-class Cohen's {kappa} 0.92, against 0.67 for the AUD diagnosis code. It agreed with one hepatologist at 0.85 on all 485 charts and with a second at 0.82 on 186 charts, on which the two hepatologists agreed at 0.87. Weighted to the registry, its sensitivity was 98% and specificity 94%, against 63% and 96% for the AUD diagnosis code, and 61% of an estimated 6,223 patients with AUD had no AUD diagnosis by the first cirrhosis diagnosis. MedDx is openly available as an off-the-shelf, equitable, and auditable tool to identify AUD.

data.summary: added: Preprint: Development of a knowledge distillation-based rapid prediction model for 7-day adverse prognosis in emergency patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding

after.title: Preprint: Development of a knowledge distillation-based rapid prediction model for 7-day adverse prognosis in emergency patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding
after.authors: Li, Z.; Guo, L.; Jing, Z.; Yan, Y.; He, J.; Xiao, H.; Zhou, Y.; Xu, T.; Qiao, W.; Duan, Q.; Wang, L.; Zhang, Y.; Chen, L.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Chinese PLA General Hospital First Medical Center
after.abstract: Background: To construct a rapid prediction model for 7-day adverse prognosis in emergency patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (AUGIB) based on feature-constrained knowledge distillation. Methods:A retrospective analysis was conducted on clinical data from 601 AUGIB patients admitted to the Emergency Department of the First Medical Center of Chinese Peoples Liberation Army (PLA) General Hospital from December 2023 to January 2025. Modeling was performed in two stages. First, a teacher model was trained using full-dimensional clinical indicators. Second, a student model (rapid prediction model) was developed. Bedside-obtainable features were selected through feature contribution analysis and physician experience, excluding hematological indicators. Knowledge distillation was introduced from the teacher model. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) served as the primary metric to select the optimal model. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used for interpretability analysis. Results:Eleven features were selected to build the rapid prediction model. The Light Gradient Boosting Model (LightGBM) model performed best with an AUC of 0.848, accuracy of 0.826, precision of 0.750, recall of 0.732, F1 score of 0.741, and Brier score of 0.128. SHAP analysis showed that Glasgow Coma Scale, age, and sex held the highest predictive value. The model relies only on immediate bedside indicators such as vital signs and comorbidities. This ensures good timeliness. Its AUC was higher than that of pre-endoscopic Rockall score, Shock Index, Age-Shock Index, and Modified Shock Index (P<0.05). Although the difference was not statistically significant, its AUC was higher than that of Glasgow-Blatchford score, AIMS-65, and Modified Early Warning Score (P>0.05). It showed clear advantages in accuracy and precision. Compared to the optimal teacher model, the AUC decreased by only 0.014, maintaining good discriminatory performance. Conclusion:This rapid prediction model possesses the capability for rapid prediction of 7-day adverse prognosis in emergency AUGIB patients while maintaining certain discriminatory performance. It assists emergency physicians in rapid decision-making and resource allocation. This helps improve prognosis and reduce medical costs.

data.summary: added: Preprint: ViDAS: Timely and Granular Estimation of Respiratory Virus Distributions in SARI Surveillance in Brazil

after.title: Preprint: ViDAS: Timely and Granular Estimation of Respiratory Virus Distributions in SARI Surveillance in Brazil
after.authors: Silva, J. F. A.; Soares, G. P.; Bastos, L. S.; Gomes, M. F. C.; Izbicki, R.
after.abstract: Effective monitoring of Severe Acute Respiratory Infections (SARI) is critical for public health but faces challenges such as reporting delays, incomplete information on negative test results, and data sparsity in specific regions and age groups. This study proposes a novel statistical framework to estimate the granular distribution of respiratory viruses among hospitalized SARI patients in Brazil. We employ Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) to model viral proportions as conditional probabilities based on patient age, location, and time. A key methodological contribution is the development of SViDAS, a semi-parametric estimator that integrates viral probabilities over continuous lognormal age distributions, enabling estimation for arbitrary age intervals. Additionally, to address the black box limitations of machine learning, we introduce an interpretability strategy based on the estimator's internal embedding space, which identifies relevant training instances to explain individual predictions. Using data from the Brazilian SIVEP-Gripe system (2022-2024), results demonstrate that our models reduce the Brier Score estimation error by approximately 40% for SARS-CoV-2 and 36% for RSV compared with the empirical aggregation benchmark. Furthermore, the reporting-delay analysis indicates that estimation error decreases sharply during the first few weeks and tends to stabilize after approximately 3 to 5 weeks for the main viruses, although the stabilization point varies by virus and geographical region. This approach provides a computationally efficient, high-resolution framework for timely surveillance of respiratory-virus distributions, including in municipalities with limited immediate data availability.

after.title: Preprint: Prenatal exposure to semi-volatile organic compounds and early childhood sleep duration
after.authors: Binczewski, N. R.; Hurst, J. H.; Lunsford-Avery, J. R.; Hoehn, R. M.; Boxer, E. F.; Stapleton, H. M.; Hoffman, K.
after.abstract: Background: Adequate sleep duration is critical for early childhood development; however, environmental determinants of sleep during this period remain understudied. Objective: We evaluated associations between prenatal exposure to semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) and parent-reported sleep duration among 147 children 2-24 months of age. Methods: Mothers in Project HOPE 1000, a prospective pregnancy cohort in central North Carolina, wore silicone wristbands for 5 days during each trimester, and 117 SVOCs were quantified. Generalized linear mixed-effects models were adjusted for child age, race, ethnicity, and an exposure-age interaction term. Results: At least 70% of wristbands had detectable levels of 36 SVOCs. Among 2-month-olds, higher prenatal exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, phthalates, and organophosphate esters was associated with decreased sleep duration across daytime, nighttime, and total sleep over a 24-hour period (e.g., benzyl butyl phthalate exposure was associated with lower expected nighttime sleep duration (Multiplicative Change: 0.77, 95% Confidence Interval: 0.61, 0.95). Results among 2-month-olds were similar when exposure was assessed as a mixture. Associations were largely null at older ages across all sleep outcomes. Significance: Prenatal SVOC exposure may have significant impacts on sleep duration during early infancy. Future studies should assess how these differences relate to broader measures of sleep health.

after.abstract: In a prolonged crisis dialogue with a large language model (LLM), a change of speaker or topic, or a pause, can leave part of the previously reported danger outside the focus of the response. A previous study of 14-turn dialogues described reactions to crisis messages; here, the subject is the subsequent history of specific people. The aim was to build a map of phenomena of person-level crisis contact from scenario circumstances, LLM responses, independent clinical judgments, and machine readings. The research design comprised 48 Ukrainian-language analytical dialogues with ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, built on 16 scenarios that unfolded over 37 turns in three rounds. Combinations of scenario conditions included different directions of danger, the appearance of new people, a change of speaker, alternation of crisis and everyday messages, returns after pauses, and an identical message repeated against a longer history. We used independent clinical assessment, repeated assessment of selected episodes, machine assessment, and pilot procedures exploring the capacities of evaluators. The primary unit of person-level analysis was the dialogue x turn x person position. Combining the procedures allowed us to trace a person's identity across a change of role, the persistence of danger after the person stopped taking part in the conversation, the coexistence of risk to self with threat to others, and how help was directed. Independent clinical assessments at turns 13-14 agreed on 88.6% of records ({kappa} = 0.65), and in a separate repeated assessment on 98.4% of comparable records ({kappa} = 0.93). The explanations of clinical decisions revealed different time horizons of assessment, different thresholds for treating indirect signs as sufficient, and anticipation of possible consequences. Machine passes revealed phenomena of identifying people and of the relation between a formal decision and its justification. In 42 pairs of responses to an identical message, a specific person was mentioned in 33 responses at turn 26 and in 26 at turn 37; the crisis was mentioned in 27 and 21, respectively. In comparing the responses, we could distinguish preserving the history, checking the current state, directing an action, and providing a crisis resource as separate functions. The reaction to a crisis message does not describe the whole contact cycle when danger concerns several people. The map of phenomena keeps the differences between clinical and machine readings as material for further refining assessment criteria and for separate tests of safety functions.

after.title: Preprint: Ambient Heat and Age-dependent Blood Pressure Responses in 184,000 U.S. Adults
after.authors: Yang, S.; Sbarra, D. A.; Klimentidis, Y. C.; Brown, H. E.
after.abstract: Aims: Extreme heat challenges cardiovascular regulation, particularly in older adults. Although blood pressure is generally lower in warmer weather, short-term within-person associations across the temperature distribution remain incompletely characterised. Methods: We linked repeated outpatient blood-pressure measurements from the All of Us Research Program to hourly ERA5-Land weather data aggregated to local calendar days. The primary exposure was maximum temperature during the complete local day preceding each visit. Models with participant and exact calendar-date fixed effects included 2,279,955 person-days from 181,865 participants for systolic blood pressure and 2,266,080 person-days from 181,770 participants for diastolic blood pressure. Results: Compared with a preceding-day maximum temperature of 18.4 degrees Celsius (50th percentile), a temperature of 31.3 degrees Celsius (95th percentile) was associated with lower systolic blood pressure (-0.66 mmHg; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.77 to -0.55) and diastolic blood pressure (-0.28 mmHg; 95% CI, -0.35 to -0.21). Associations extended through the 99th percentile. The systolic difference between these two temperatures became 0.20 mmHg more negative per decade of age and reached -0.99 mmHg at age 75. Social-material vulnerability and long-term climate showed little evidence of modifying the associations, and the inverse associations persisted after adjustment for wildfire smoke. In secondary analyses, visit-to-visit blood-pressure variability showed little overall association with heat, although the heat-associated difference in absolute changes between successive systolic readings increased by 0.05 mmHg per decade of age. Conclusion: Preceding-day heat was associated with modestly lower outpatient blood pressure within individuals, with stronger associations at older ages.

after.title: Preprint: Effects of Internet Adoption on Depressive Scores and Self-Rated Health in China: Multi-Period Difference-in-Differences Analysis
after.authors: Yun, Y.; Zhang, Y. D.
after.abstract: Abstract Background: Internet use has grown rapidly worldwide over the past decades. Extensive research has explored the health implications of internet use across diverse demographic groups, but most existing studies rely on associational designs. Evidence on the population-level causal effects of internet adoption on both psychological well-being and overall health status remains limited, particularly in settings where individuals adopt the internet across different time points. Objective: This study aimed to investigate the dynamic causal effects of internet adoption on both depressive scores and self-rated health among baseline internet nonusers in China. Methods: This study used longitudinal data from 4 waves of the China Family Panel Studies spanning 2016-2022. Participants who were internet nonusers at the 2016 baseline and provided complete responses across all 4 waves were included, whereas those who ever discontinued internet use after initial adoption were excluded. Internet use was assessed via self-reported questionnaires, depressive scores were evaluated using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale Short Form (CES-D 8), and overall health status was measured using self-rated health on a 5-point scale. A Difference-in-Differences framework with multiple time periods was applied to estimate the causal effects of internet adoption on both outcomes under the conditional parallel trends assumption. Robustness checks and mechanism analyses were further conducted to verify result validity and explore underlying pathways. Results: A total of 4026 participants were included in the analysis. Internet adoption reduced depressive scores on the CES-D 8 scale under a simple weighted average of all group-time average treatment effects (overall ATT = -0.302, SE = 0.156, P < .10), whereas event-study aggregation across post-adoption periods revealed a statistically significant cumulative reduction that intensified with longer exposure durations (overall dynamic ATT = -0.354, SE = 0.179, P < .05). In contrast, the average treatment effect on self-rated health was not statistically different from 0 (overall ATT = 0.039, SE = 0.046). Mechanism analyses suggested that internet adoption may have lowered depressive scores through expanded engagement in media entertainment, more frequent physical exercise, and higher total family expenditure, whereas the physiological gains of physical exercise may have been offset by prolonged sedentary behavior and health-compromising habits such as smoking. Robustness checks confirmed that these findings were not driven by random chance or sample selection bias. Conclusions: This study demonstrated that among baseline internet nonusers in China, internet adoption generated a cumulative reduction in depressive scores relative to what would have happened in the absence of internet adoption, yet had no statistically significant effect on self-rated health. Future public health initiatives should prioritize inclusive digital infrastructure expansion and age-friendly adaptations alongside fostering digital health literacy, curating health-oriented online content, and implementing targeted measures to mitigate the physiological risks of sedentary behavior and health-compromising habits.

after.authors: Kim, H.-K.; Hamada, Y.; Hatamoto, Y.; Hatanaka, M.; Nanri, H.; Nakagata, T.; Chen, Y.-A.; Matsumoto, N.; Shimoda, S.; Tanaka, S.; Miyachi, M.; Tahara, Y.; Shibata, S.; Yoshimura, E.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Center for Clinical Nutrition, National Institutes of Biomedical Innovation, Health and Nutrition
after.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between differences in physical activity patterns and blood glucose variability under free-living conditions in healthy adults. A total of 102 adult participants (60 women, 42 men; age [≥]20years) wore a triaxial accelerometer for one week to record physical activity. Participants were then categorized into three groups based on the predominant time of day of physical activity: morning (06:00-12:00), afternoon (12:00-18:00), and night (18:00-24:00). Continuous glucose monitoring was used to assess blood glucose variability. Additionally, a prescribed breakfast was served on Day 1 of the experiment, and blood glucose fluctuations were assessed up to 2 hours after consumption. 24-hour blood glucose variability differed according to physical activity patterns, with the evening group having a lower 24-hour blood glucose variability than the morning and afternoon groups. In addition, the night group (127.7 {+/-} 9.4 ml/dl) had significantly lower values 45 minutes after the prescribed meal than the morning (149.3 {+/-} 9.5 ml/dl) and afternoon groups (146.7 {+/-} 5.6 ml/dl) (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that engaging in physical activity during the evening is associated with reduced daily blood glucose fluctuations and smaller post-meal glucose spikes in healthy adults.

after.abstract: Purpose: To develop and evaluate DeTangle, a deep learning-based method for cardiac computed tomography (CT) deblurring using internally estimated deformation-magnitude maps and single-phase reconstructed images. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 60 patients (median age, 61 years; 40 males) who underwent cardiac CT between January 2024 and October 2025. Patients comprised training, validation, and internal test sets (30, five, and 25 patients, respectively). DeTangle jointly optimizes deformation-map estimation and restoration using privileged deformation information during training but requires only target-phase reconstructed images at inference. Full reconstructions (250 ms) served as inputs and half reconstructions (66 ms) as references. The structural similarity index measure (SSIM) was assessed in 424 test phases. DeTangle and the image-only Baseline were compared using five-point visual scores in 200 phases and edge measurements in 100 phases. Patient-clustered generalized estimating equations incorporated Holm adjustment. Results: Mean SSIM ({+/-} SD) was higher with DeTangle than Baseline (0.972 {+/-} 0.006 vs 0.968 {+/-} 0.008, P < .001). Mean coronary and left ventricular myocardial scores were also higher (3.3 {+/-} 1.0 vs 2.9 {+/-} 1.1 and 4.2 {+/-} 1.0 vs 3.5 {+/-} 1.3, respectively; both P < .001). DeTangle increased edge rise slope and reduced edge rise distance at the interventricular septum and right and left coronary arteries (all P < .05). At least one primary visual score was lower with DeTangle than with Baseline in nine of 200 phases (4.5%). Conclusion: DeTangle improved reference-image agreement, coronary and myocardial visual scores, and edge sharpness versus Baseline, although some phases showed localized image-quality deterioration.

after.authors: Stikker, B. S.; Junqueira-Neto, S.; Draijer, S.; Eijk, P. P.; Ferro, A.; Egthuijsen, J.; Pronk, M.; Verburg, N.; Sie, D.; Maas, S. L. N.; Bos, E.; Pinheiro, J.; Oliveira, R.; Pinto, M.; de Ridder, J.; Vermeulen, C.; Wesseling, P.; Lima, J.; Ylstra, B.; Kooi, E.-J.

after.abstract: Background: Array-based methylation profiling with the Heidelberg classifier supports WHO-CNS5 classification of CNS tumors, but its substantial hands-on time, cost, centralized infrastructure and dependence on externally-hosted software limit broad implementation. Nanopore methylation sequencing combined with AI-based classification is a viable alternative, yet performance evidence required for implementation in adult CNS tumor diagnostics is limited. We test the equivalence of nanopore methylation profiling using the Sturgeon-v2 classifier against a WHO-CNS5-compliant integrated reference diagnosis incorporating array-based classification. Methods: We compared Sturgeon-v2 classifications from nanopore sequencing of fresh-frozen tissue DNA with array-based reference diagnoses of matched FFPE tissue DNA, in two cohorts of 154 and 47 primary CNS tumors. Nanopore-derived copy-number alteration (CNA) profiles complemented Sturgeon-v2 predictions to resolve low-confidence calls. CNA-derived tumor cell fractions and histopathological evaluation determined tissue adequacy. Outcomes were categorized as concordant; discordant; additional analyses needed; or tissue inadequate for methylation profiling. Equivalence required the 95% upper confidence limit (95UCL) for discordance to be below 10%. Sturgeon-v2 classification and CNA analysis were implemented in the containerized pipeline NEURON. Results: No discordant outcomes were observed (95UCL: 1.7%), with consistent performance across cohorts. Of 201 samples, 26 were inadequate due to low tumor purity or poor tissue quality. Of the remaining 175 samples, 167 were concordant with the reference diagnosis; eight required additional analyses. Conclusion: Diagnostic equivalence and reproducibility across independent cohorts, together with the publicly available, locally-executable NEURON workflow, provide evidence and tools to support laboratory validation, accreditation and routine implementation of nanopore methylation profiling for adult CNS tumor classification.

after.abstract: Purpose To quantify how CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) reports documented right ventricular (RV) strain and the RV-to-left ventricular (LV) diameter ratio in acute pulmonary embolism (PE) before the 2026 multisociety reporting recommendation. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1,534 CTPA reports from MIMIC-IV-Ext-PE (2008-2022), one per patient. Rule-based extraction classified overall strain statements and identified four CT features. A physician reviewed all 22 reports flagged for RV/LV ratio wording and independently coded a random held-out sample of 100 reports. Multivariable logistic regression, including approximate examination period, assessed factors associated with documentation gaps. Results Five reports (0.3%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.1-0.8%) gave an exact RV/LV ratio, and seven (0.5%) gave a threshold or range. Of 412 reports (26.9%) without an overall strain statement, 39 documented at least one coded CT feature. In total, 373 reports (24.3%, 95% CI 22.2-26.5%) documented neither. Isolated subsegmental PE was associated with higher adjusted odds of lacking an overall statement (odds ratio 2.76, 95% CI 2.02-3.78). These odds declined over time (2020-2022 vs 2008-2010: 0.14, 95% CI 0.06-0.31), and the association with a structured organ-system heading attenuated after this adjustment (0.99, 95% CI 0.69-1.43). Agreement with manual physician coding in classifying overall strain statements was 93.0% (Cohen's kappa 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.97). Conclusion Exact RV/LV ratios were rarely documented, and nearly one quarter of reports contained neither an overall strain statement nor any of the four CT features. Omission declined over time. These estimates provide a single-center baseline for evaluating uptake of the 2026 recommendation.

after.title: Preprint: Conditional normative modeling of whole-body FDG PET/CT: inter-organ relationships outperform reference-region normalization for label-free detection of lesion-bearing organs
after.authors: Park, C.-h.; Park, H.-J.
after.abstract: Purpose. Reading whole-body 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-D-glucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) means judging each organ's uptake against what is expected for that patient. Clinical criteria do this with a single reference region, the liver or the blood pool. We tested whether a normative model conditioned on all other organs detects lesion-bearing organs better than reference-region normalization, without lesion labels. Methods. We analyzed the public autoPET FDG PET/CT dataset (1,014 studies; 896 patients with age and sex, 412 without malignant lesions). Models trained on control patients predicted the log maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of each of 34 organs, segmented with TotalSegmentator on CT, from age, sex, and the median uptake of the other organs on eroded masks, without lesion labels, which served only as the reference standard. Out-of-fold deviation scores were compared with SUVmax, liver- and blood-pool-referenced, and age-sex normative scores for detecting organs with [≥] 2 ml of lesion (1,700 organs, 355 patients). Secondary analyses included false positives per patient, repeat scans, and residual soft-tissue regions. Results. Other organs explained a median 67% of the between-patient variance in uptake, against 34% for global uptake with age and sex. The conditional linear model outperformed liver referencing: the within-patient area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.916 vs 0.902 (difference 0.014, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.007-0.021), the false-positive rate at 90% sensitivity fell from 0.33 to 0.27, and at 80% sensitivity 2.9 instead of 4.3 lesion-free organs per patient were flagged. A global-uptake reference gained little (AUC 0.907). The advantage was robust to analysis choices, including a peak SUV target, and to lesion-cleaned inputs, and leveled off at about 200 training controls. Gradient boosting did not improve on the linear model, whereas modeling patient-specific variance made calibration uniform across patients. Conditional scores changed organ by organ between repeat scans, and the gain extended to mediastinal but not abdominal or pelvic soft tissue. Conclusion. Conditioning an organ's expected uptake on the patient's other organs generalizes reference-region normalization and reduces false positives in label-free detection of abnormal organ uptake, using oncology controls rather than healthy volunteers. Organ-level conditional deviations provide a calibrated, patient-specific reference on which voxel-level localization within organs can build.

after.authors: Ouyang, N.; Han, L.; Abel, E.; DeRycke, E.; Kinder, D.; Moreines, L. T.; Redeker, N. S.; Curry, L. A.; Luhrs, C.; levy, c.; Ibarra, J.; Kavalieratos, D.; Akgün, K.; Allen, L. A.; Feder, S. L.
after.abstract: Background: Days spent at home and hospice enrollment describe different but potentially related aspects of high-quality end-of-life care for people with advanced heart failure (aHF). However, how much variation in these quality outcomes exists and what drives between-facility differences is unknown. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included people with aHF at 119 Veterans Affairs medical centers (VAMCs) who died in 2022-2023. Outcomes were days at home during the last 90 days of life and hospice enrollment. Multilevel linear and logistic regression models with facility random intercepts quantified between-facility variation before and after adjustment for patient characteristics, facility complexity, and facility volume. Results: The cohort included 10,114 decedents (mean [standard deviation, SD] age, 76.5 [9.6] years; 98.2% male). Patients spent a mean (SD) of 59.4 (29.9) days at home during their final 90 days of life, and 4521 (44.7%) enrolled in hospice. For days at home, the adjusted intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was 0.95%. The adjusted median difference between two randomly selected VAMCs was 2.7 days (95% CI, 2.0-3.7). Measured patient and facility characteristics explained 29% of the between-facility variance. For hospice enrollment, the adjusted ICC was 3.6%. The adjusted median odds ratio was 1.40 (95% CI, 1.31-1.51), indicating a median 40% higher odds of hospice use when comparing two similar patients treated at two randomly selected VAMCs. Between-facility variance increased 15.0% after adjustment for patient characteristics, facility complexity, and volume. Conclusions: People with aHF spent one-third of their final 90 days of life in institutional settings; fewer than half received hospice. Adjusted home time differed little across VAMCs, while hospice enrollment varied substantially. Persistent variation in hospice enrollment suggests that interventions targeting facility-level care processes, such as referral practices, could improve hospice utilization among people with aHF.

L.; Adarve-Castro, A.; Gonzalez-Manzanares, R.; Berteli-Garcia, G.; Costa, F.; Carmona-Segovia, A.; Molina-Ramos, A. I.; Rodriguez-Capitan, J.; Jimenez-Navarro, M. F.; Pavon-Moron, F. J.

after.abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) reflects atherosclerotic burden. We examined whether peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) expression of calcium-regulatory and chemotactic-receptor genes and plasma chemokine concentrations were associated with CAC presence and with its extent among adults with detectable calcification. Methods: This single-center, cross-sectional study included 53 adults undergoing coronary computed tomography, 27 with CAC=0 and 26 with CAC>0. We measured 10 PBMC transcripts by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction and 8 plasma chemokines by multiplex immunoassay. We assessed associations using permutation tests, composite indices, and compartment-specific principal component analyses. Results: All 10 PBMC transcripts correlated positively with CAC after false discovery rate correction. Associations were strongest for S100A9 (rho=+0.69), S100A8 and CXCR2 (both rho=+0.66), and CCR2 (rho=+0.65). Plasma CX3CL1, CXCL2, CXCL16, and CXCL12 were lower in participants with detectable CAC, whereas CXCL1 was higher and correlated with PBMC CXCR2 expression (rho=+0.66, p<0.001). Most molecular differences distinguished participants with and without CAC. In exploratory analyses among participants with detectable CAC, CCR2 expression (rho=+0.43, p=0.043), the chemotactic-receptor index (rho=0.51, p=0.022), and plasma CXCL1 (rho=+0.42, p=0.034) correlated with CAC burden. Additional adjustment for diabetes or hypertension attenuated selected associations. Conclusions: Detectable coronary calcification was associated with coordinated differences in PBMC gene expression and a distinct plasma chemokine profile. CCR2 expression, the receptor index, and plasma CXCL1 warrant further study in relation to the extent of calcification.

after.authors: Paulus, M. P.; Kuplicki, R.; Yeh, H.-W.; Gross, E. C.
after.abstract: Metabolic interventions are being investigated for major depressive disorder (MDD), but evidence for specific formulations remains limited. This double-masked, placebo-controlled randomized trial evaluates a multicomponent formulation containing D-{beta}-hydroxybutyrate (D-BHB), micronutrients, and metabolic cofactors for 8 weeks. The registered primary outcome is week 8 nucleus accumbens blood-oxygen-level-dependent response during Monetary Incentive Delay reward anticipation; the secondary outcome is medial prefrontal response during self-referential processing. Here, we report an exploratory Bayesian interim analysis of 62 individuals screened, 29 randomized (active, n=15; placebo, n=14), 26 who received at least one dose (safety population), and 22 who were evaluable (active, n=10; placebo, n=12). D-BHB rose after week 8 dosing in the active arm but not placebo. The primary week 8 active-minus-placebo estimate was 0.02 (95% credible interval [CrI], -0.12 to 0.17); the difference in change was 0.00 (-0.17 to 0.18). The covariate-adjusted secondary estimates were 0.03 (-0.13 to 0.18) at week 8 and 0.00 (-0.18 to 0.17) for change. Exploratory clinician-rated symptoms favored active treatment (MADRS week 8 difference, -7.28 [-12.00 to -2.47]), whereas self-reported symptoms were uncertain (QIDS-SR16, -1.95 [-5.13 to 1.15]). Three of 26 exposed participants reported four mild adverse events; none was serious or judged treatment-related. The formulation increased circulating D-BHB, but engagement of the prespecified imaging targets was not demonstrated. The exploratory clinician-rated symptom signal requires confirmation and cannot be attributed to D-BHB alone.

after.authors: Royal, S. S.; Yousup, S.; Azad, M. A. K.; Uddin, M. S.; Zarin, T.; Nahiduzzaman, F.; Islam, M. A.; Haque, M. A.
after.abstract: Microbiological safety and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in street-vended foods remain insufficiently characterized in Bangladeshs secondary towns. To assess bacterial contamination, antimicrobial susceptibility and hygiene-associated contamination factors in Habiganj municipality. A cross-sectional study conducted during June - September surveyed 110 vendors at eight sites and examined 219 food, water and surface samples; 99 isolates underwent susceptibility testing against 13 antimicrobials. Analyses included multivariable logistic regression with vendor-clustered standard errors, Spearman correlation, principal component analysis (PCA) and hygiene-profile clustering. Overall, 35.6% of samples contained Escherichia coli, Salmonella spp. or Staphylococcus aureus, and 41.6% were microbiologically unsatisfactory. Multivariable analysis identified higher contamination odds among vendors who never covered food (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 5.16; p < 0.001), sometimes covered food (AOR 2.67; p = 0.035), or washed hands irregularly (AOR 2.08; p = 0.046), relative to consistent covering and regular handwashing, respectively. Hygiene-practice scores correlated inversely with mean total plate count (Spearmans {rho} = -0.26; p < 0.05), whereas food-holding time showed no correlation ({rho} = 0.01; p = 0.897). The first two principal components explained 22.5% of hygiene-indicator variance; two weakly separated vendor clusters had comparable contamination prevalence (38.8% versus 34.2%; p = 0.616). Among isolates, 55.6% were multidrug resistant, resistance was highest to ampicillin (62.6%), and tetracycline-doxycycline exhibited the strongest co-resistance ({phi} = 0.73). Frequent bacterial contamination and multidrug resistance warrant municipal interventions emphasizing consistent food covering, regular handwashing and integrated food-chain AMR surveillance.

after.authors: Hosking, A.; Samarasekera, N.; Loan, J. J.; Moullaali, T. J.; Rodrigues, M.; Rannikmae, K.; Smith, C.; Seth, S.; Whiteley, W. N.; Al-Shahi Salman, R.

after.abstract: Background: The global burden of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) remains high. Identifying trends in incidence and outcome requires resource-intensive epidemiological surveillance. Our objective was to characterise incidence, survival and functional outcome of people with ICH in a cohort study; and compare to healthcare systems data (HSD) in the same region. Methods: We conducted a prospective population-based inception cohort study in Lothian, Scotland, UK (the Lothian Audit of Treatment of ICH, LATCH). LATCH included all spontaneous non-traumatic ICH in Lothian residents [≥]16 years between 1st June 2010 - 31st May 2013 and 1st November 2018 - 31st October 2021. We identified and characterized people with ICH in HSD in the same region and period using linked primary and secondary care records, community prescriptions and death records. We calculated incidence per 100,000 person-years; 30-day survival; and sensitivity and positive predictive value of ICH detection in HSD. For functional outcome one year after ICH, we compared the modified Rankin Scale score (mRS) in LATCH to days alive and out of hospital in HSD. Results: In LATCH, from 1283 possible cases, 1021 were first-ever ICH. We identified 876 people with ICH in HSD in the same period. In LATCH, ICH incidence was 23.7 (95%CI 22.2-25.2) per 100,000 person-years (48.5% male, mean age 72 (SD 14.6) years), with no time trend (trend in crude incidence rates 0.31/year (-3.78-4.39)). ICH incidence in HSD was 23.1 (21.6-24.6) per 100,000 person-years (48.3% male, mean age 74.2 (SD 14.0) years). The positive predictive value of ICH identified in HSD versus LATCH was 78.3% (75.4%-81.0%). 30-day case fatality was 41.2% (38.1%-44.2%) in LATCH and 39.0% (35.5%-42.3%) in HSD. We found good correlation between functional outcome measures (Spearman's r=0.88, p<0.001). Conclusions: The burden of ICH remains persistently high. HSD appears accurate for assessing incidence, survival and functional outcome.

after.abstract: Background. Long-term functional outcomes after exposure to rovunaptabin (BC007) in patients with post-COVID syndrome (PCS) still remain elusive. Methods. We compared 24 participants previously exposed to rovunaptabin in the phase IIa reCOVer trial with 64 independently recruited participants of disCOVer study who had never received rovunaptabin. All had PCS with fatigue and functional autoantibodies against G-protein-coupled receptors. Median follow-up from baseline was 267.5 and 278 days, respectively. We compared follow-up Bell scores using analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline Bell score, age, and sex. Other patient-reported outcomes were summarized descriptively in the previously exposed cohort. Findings. Mean Bell scores increased from 34.58 to 51.25 in the rovunaptabin exposed cohort and from 40.47 to 46.25 in the rovunaptabin-naive cohort. The adjusted difference in follow-up Bell score was 9.71 points in favor of the exposed cohort (95% CI 1.80-17.63, p = 0.017). This cohort showed an increased mean FACIT-Fatigue score by 9.71 points and the mean Fatigue Severity Scale score decreased by 1.02 points. Interpretation. Prior one-time rovunaptabin exposure was associated with better self-reported functional status at approximately nine months after rovunaptabin exposure. Controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to assess whether rovunaptabin produces lasting functional benefit, even when administered multiple times.
